errorCodes.meaning: A payload member is well-formed against the schema but unusable for this request — the `messageHash` length does not match `hashAlgorithm`, or `algorithm` is incompatible with the key's `keyType`. See [category conventions](../../_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md#1-family-error-codes).
The named key exists but its `status` is not `active`, so it cannot sign.

algorithm.description: The algorithm the signature was made with — the one the request named.

schema.description: A request for an SSHSIG signature (the OpenSSH `PROTOCOL.sshsig` format git uses for SSH commit signing) over a message digest, made with a key the custodian holds. The producer supplies the digest and the namespace; the custodian builds the signed-data structure itself. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

algorithm.description: Signature algorithm, as a JOSE identifier: `EdDSA` with an `ed25519` key (SSH key type `ssh-ed25519`), `ES256` with a `p256` key (`ecdsa-sha2-nistp256`). These are the custodian-held key types SSHSIG defines a signature for. MUST be compatible with the named key's `keyType`. Closed: an unrecognised algorithm is refused, never substituted.

hashAlgorithm.description: The digest algorithm the producer applied to the message, in the SSHSIG spelling (externally owned, carried verbatim). It is written into the signed data, so the verifier recomputes the digest with the same algorithm.

keyId.description: Identifier of the key to sign with. The key MUST be `active`.

messageHash.description: The digest of the message, `H(message)` in `PROTOCOL.sshsig`, base64url-encoded without padding: 32 bytes (43 characters) for `sha256`, 64 bytes (86 characters) for `sha512`. The custodian never sees the message itself.

namespace.description: The SSHSIG namespace the signature is bound to — `git` for a git commit or tag, `file` for `ssh-keygen -Y sign` over a file. Printable ASCII without spaces. A signature made under one namespace does not verify under another, so the custodian MAY restrict which namespaces a producer may name.
